meta.title: Dress Right Clothing Corp. — Phase 1.5: Adjustment Recognition
meta.description: Review the unadjusted trial balance from Phase 1. Flag accounts that need adjusting entries and identify the adjustment type before recording them in Phase 2.
learning_objectives: Scan an unadjusted trial balance to identify accounts that need adjustment
Classify each adjustment by type (asset-to-expense, liability-to-revenue, accrued expense, depreciation)
Explain why each adjustment is needed before recording it

signals.reason: Supplies were purchased but some have been consumed during the period. A physical count shows $1,200 remaining, so $800 has been used.
signals.hint: Physical count on July 31 reveals $1,200 remaining

signals.reason: Rent was prepaid for 12 months on July 1. One month has expired, so $2,000 must be recognized as rent expense.
Long-term assets must be depreciated over their useful life. Monthly depreciation = $12,000 ÷ 60 months = $200.
Cash was received in advance for 2 months of sublease. By July 31, half a month of service has been provided, so $250 has been earned.
Interest has accrued on the $40,000 notes payable since July 1. One month of interest at 10% = $333.
Employees earned salaries in the second half of July that have not yet been paid. Accrued salaries = $5,500.
signals.hint: Second half of July salaries unpaid
